newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korean petrol prices fall slightly.
newsitem.headline: South Korean petrol prices fall slightly.

text.p: Petrol prices at South Korean pumps currently average at 845-846 won a litre, down slightly from 848-850 won last month, oil industry officials said on Friday.
Oil refiners and government officials said the petrol prices were reduced to reflect a fall in global crude oil prices.
But some refiners said the cut was also to avoid a consumer backlash following a continuous rise in the prices after deregulation on January 1.
Consumers paid 815 won for a litre of petrol at the end of 1996.
"Crude oil prices have fallen but not enough to offset the loss from the won's depreciation against the dollar," said an oil company official.
"We've decided to cut the price to avoid angering consumers by raising the price for three months in a row."
Prices of kerosene and diesel also dropped this month, refiners said.
From January 1, domestic prices of gasoline, kerosene, diesel and C-type fuel were deregulated and are no longer subject to a government-set monthly price ceiling.
